correctness.rationale: For the exact multiplication table, the right multiplication commutators yield the right Leibniz identity. On the quotient by the product span, invertibility and [U,U]=0 force a=U1 and b=V2 nonzero. The symmetrized product and [[V,U],U]=0 force U5=U7=0. At that point [U,V]=−ab e3, so the symmetrized relation forces the e8 component of [V,U] to vanish; this justifies the step used to solve for V7. Equality of [φ(e5),V] and [φ(e6),V] gives a=3V1+b. Independently checked sufficiency from the three possible nonzero right slots: right multiplication by Y is Y1 R1+Y2 R2+Y3 R3; substituting the displayed columns into those three operators gives the generator images and all other defining products, and the higher slots are zero. Only 2, 3 and nonzero torus coordinates need be inverted. The block diagonal yields the eight weights and determinant a^6 b^15. For b not in μ2∪μ3, the four forbidden a's are distinct, and the extra quadratic roots exist exactly for square b and cannot coincide with any of the four. The square count n/2−g−ε and resulting quadratic prove the formula, the 5/7 boundary and the density limit. The independent branch check (branches/15be6f16-7356-47d7-bafe-a32ae7d4318c/independent_check.py) found the plus-sign residual at p=7 and matched the torus count at all even orders 4 through 120. These finite checks supplement the proof. Uploaded scripts and recorded output were inspected, not run.
